judgments.reason: 'oliguria' is present literally in the vignette and supports AKI, but it does not specifically support rhabdomyolysis as the etiology; it is a sign of renal impairment from any cause.

'red-colored urine' is present literally in the vignette and clinically supports myoglobinuria from rhabdomyolysis (confirmed by absence of red cells on urinalysis), directly supporting the rhabdomyolysis etiology.

'reduced ionized calcium 8.16 mg/dL' is present literally in the vignette; hypocalcemia is a recognized metabolic consequence of rhabdomyolysis due to calcium deposition in necrotic muscle, supporting the rhabdomyolysis etiology.

'elevated phosphate 5.4 mg/dL' is present literally in the vignette; hyperphosphatemia results from release of intracellular phosphate from damaged muscle cells, clinically supporting rhabdomyolysis as the etiology.

'Serum creatine phosphokinase was markedly elevated at over 90,000 U/L' is present literally in the vignette and is the hallmark laboratory finding of rhabdomyolysis, directly supporting the etiology modifier.
